claim: Château des Ducs de Savoie museum is free entry, open Tue-Fri 14h-18h and 10h-13h/14h-18h on weekends/holidays/summer school breaks; guided tour of Sainte-Chapelle runs 04/05-23/06/2026 Tue-Thu from 14h30 with booking required, 5.50-7.50€.
quote: Entrée gratuite. Ouvert le mardi, mercredi, jeudi et vendredi de 14h à 18h. Les jours fériés, week-ends et vacances scolaires d'été de 10h à 13h et de 14h à 18h.

claim: The Fontaine des Éléphants was built in 1838 in tribute to General de Boigne, a Chambéry benefactor; it stands 17.65 m tall with four cast-iron elephants arranged as a cross of Savoy.
quote: This fountain was built in 1838 to pay tribute to General de Boigne, a major benefactor of Chambéry, his native town. The fountain shows in its plane a cross of Savoy, represented by four elephants united by their rump.

claim: The Musée Savoisien reopened after an 8-year closure and major renovation, housed in a 13th-century former Franciscan convent, with a refreshed scenography of films, interactive displays and handle-able objects; admission is free.
quote: the Musée Savoisien, the departmental museum of the history and cultures of Savoie, reopened its doors to the public after eight years of closure for major works

claim: Chambéry to Jongieux is roughly 25 km by road and about 27 minutes' drive, primarily via Route du Tunnel and the D210, putting Chambéry within the 30 km radius from Jongieux.
quote: The driving distance from Chambéry to Jongieux is 25.2 kilometers and takes approximately 27 minutes. The route is primarily via Route du Tunnel and D 210.

claim: The Musée des Beaux-Arts opens daily except Mondays and public holidays 10h-18h (extended to 20h on the first Thursday of each month), with permanent collection access free; its strength is 14th-18th c. Italian schools (Sienese Bartolo di Fredi, Florentine Santi di Tito, Neapolitan Baroque Luca Giordano).
quote: Italian works from the 14th to 18th centuries are particularly well represented, with a chronological tour... Sienese school (Bartolo di Fredi), the Florentine school (Santi di Tito), and Neapolitan Baroque (Luca Giordano)

claim: Les Charmettes, Rousseau's house museum at 890 chemin des Charmettes, opens Tue-Sun 10h-18h from 1 April to 31 October and weekends only in winter; gardens are free year-round.
quote: From April 1st to October 31st: Open Tuesday to Sunday from 10am to 6pm. Closed on Mondays and public holidays. From November 1st to March 31st: Open on weekends from 10am to 6pm.

claim: The covered Halles de Chambéry market runs Tuesday-Saturday 6h-13h30; Place de Genève hosts an open-air food market Saturday morning and Tuesday 7h-12h, plus a Wed-evening market (April-October 16h-20h) limited to organic/short-supply-chain producers within 30 km of Chambéry.
quote: Tuesday Market: Place de Genève, every Tuesday from 7h to 12h... Wednesday Evening Market: From April 1st to the end of October 2026, the market runs from 16h to 20h... organic agriculture and short supply chains (30 km maximum around Chambéry). Saturday Market: Food producers occupy Place de Genève on Saturday.

claim: La Maniguette par Epicurieux, at 99 Rue Juiverie in the historic centre, is a natural-wine bar and restaurant open Tue-Sat lunch 12h-13h30 with a 15€ lunch menu and 400+ wine references.
quote: Located at 99 Rue Juiverie, La Maniguette is situated in the heart of Chambéry's historic center... lunch menu is available for €15... open Tuesday to Saturday at lunchtime from 12pm to 1:30pm

claim: Chambéry old town is a network of paved streets, covered passages and arcades; Rue de Boigne (the 'porticos') links the château to the Fontaine des Éléphants, while Place Saint-Léger is the main pedestrian artery and natural starting point for a walking tour.
quote: Rue de Boigne, which connects the castle to the Fountain of Elephants, is renowned for its arcades and shops. These arcades are nicknamed 'the porticos' by locals.

claim: The Cathédrale métropolitaine Saint-François-de-Sales features extensive trompe-l'œil frescoes covering its interior, the largest such painted surface of any French cathedral.
quote: The Cathedral of Saint-François-de-Sales, with its trompe-l'oeil frescoes, is another treasure not to miss.
